decisions.quote:
This work replicated the findings of

Murphy and colleagues (2023) where method factors account for much if not all of the observed

discriminant validity between need satisfaction and need frustration distinctions. Expanding on

Murphy and colleagues' (2023) work, these analyses clarif y, in a general population sample, that
satisfaction–frustration distinctions are overestimated in raw correlations due to Halo response

bias (dissimilar valence).
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding classify this study as a replication. Primary text confirms that Payne and Schimmack (2025) collected new survey data from a UK general-population sample (N = 749 recruited via Prolific, lines 454-466) and used confirmatory factor analysis with external Big Five personality validators to re-test the published finding of the dependent original study, Murphy et al. (2023, Psychological Assessment, 10.1037/pas0001193), which had found in student datasets that shared-method factors account for the apparent discriminant validity between need satisfaction and need frustration in the BPNSFS (with the authors concluding that their results successfully replicated Murphy et al.'s finding).
